answer: The MCP bridge exposes eleven read tools, all requiring the mcp:read scope.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects visible to the caller.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the current projection (latest per stream).

tools.name: get_series
tools.description: Read a variable's series over a window.

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: List a project's integrations, secrets redacted.

tools.name: get_integration
tools.description: Read one integration by id, secrets redacted.

notes: Read tools sit behind GET /v1/mcp/read; mcp:read projects to the 'read' capability.

answer: The MCP bridge exposes twelve write tools, all requiring the mcp:manage scope.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project owned by the caller.

tools.name: set_variable
tools.description: Set or clear a project variable's value.

tools.name: emit_event
tools.description: Emit a discrete event that can fire automations.

notes: POST /v1/mcp/write additionally requires the mcp_write_enabled flag.

answer: No. There is deliberately no delete tool on the MCP surface, and no mcp:write scope.
notes: Deleting a project stays a human, owner-only admin action (DELETE /v1/admin/projects/:proj).

answer: Health and version are unauthenticated; telemetry is ingested at POST /v1/telemetry and read per project.
notes: GET /v1/projects/:proj/state and GET /v1/projects/:proj/variables/:key/series carry the reads; the retired /v1/telemetry/:proj form does not exist.

answer: Downlink is GET /v1/control plus POST /v1/control/ack; OTA is GET /v1/ota and GET /v1/ota/image; admin mutations are DELETE /v1/admin/projects/:proj and POST /v1/admin/projects/:proj/firmware.
The MCP gate serves GET /v1/mcp/read and POST /v1/mcp/write; integrations expose GET /v1/integrations and POST /v1/integrations/test.
notes: There is no /v1/mcp/delete route; the bridge's verbs are tools, served through the two gate paths above.

answer: A series window defaults to 3600000 ms and is capped at 2592000000 ms; a firmware upload is capped at 8388608 bytes.
notes: The 8 MiB cap is MAX_FIRMWARE_BYTES in domains/firmware/upload.ts.

answer: Roles rank member < admin < owner (1/2/3); project:delete requires owner and member:invite requires admin.
notes: Permissions are a minimum-role table consulted by can(role, action).
